name: PHP-FPM smuggling
tile_line: Only if FastCGI connections are reused. Exploit public.
tldr: A PHP-FPM bug can let an attacker with no login hide a second request and run code. Public test code, no attacks. Only if the web server reuses FPM connections (off by default) and the app leaves the body unread; PHP's 19 Nov 2026 releases fix it.
summary: PHP rates it Critical (CVSS 9.2), and public test code runs PHP on a target. The reuse settings to look for are `fastcgi_keep_conn on` in nginx and `enablereuse=on` in Apache's `mod_proxy_fcgi`.

affected.label: PHP-FPM older than the 19 Nov 2026 fix
affected.text: Below 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36. PHP 8.6.0 (19 Nov) is fixed. PHP says the bug has been in the code since 5.6.0, so older, unsupported PHP is affected too. The code-execution attack needs PHP-FPM; with LiteSpeed's LSAPI it only breaks later requests. Distros may backport the fix without changing the version number.

affected.label: The web server reuses FPM connections
affected.text: nginx with `fastcgi_keep_conn on`, Apache `mod_proxy_fcgi` with `enablereuse=on`, or HAProxy keeping FastCGI connections open. Both nginx and Apache close the connection by default, which is not affected, but Apache's own PHP-FPM example turns reuse on. PHP's advisory doesn't mention Caddy. For Apache, look for `enablereuse=on` in your config.

affected.label: The app leaves the body unread
affected.text: Some code path opens `php://input` and doesn't read it to the end. PHP says frameworks that open the input stream before routing or login checks can be affected; public test code worked against an unmodified Slim 4 app. Reading the body fully avoids it, but PHP says that isn't reliable on its own.

do.label: Update PHP and restart FPM
do.text: Update to 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36 (19 Nov 2026), then restart PHP-FPM. Debian has fixed packages (DSA-6641-1 for Debian 13, DLA-4916-1 for Debian 12); Ubuntu's supported releases were still "needs evaluation" on 20 Nov.

do.label: Turn off connection reuse
do.text: Until you've updated: in nginx, remove `fastcgi_keep_conn on` (off is the default); in Apache, remove `enablereuse=on`. Then reload the web server.

do.label: Keep PHP-FPM off the network
do.text: Don't let untrusted networks reach PHP-FPM's port or socket directly.

sources.title: PHP GHSA-qc49: full advisory, affected setups, mitigations
